subject: ventures/uk-dividend-tax-calculator
professional: a UK chartered tax adviser (CTA) or ACCA who prepares Self Assessment returns for owner-managed company directors; first checks: is dividend income taxed last on top of non-savings income (ITA 2007 s16), does the 500 GBP dividend allowance still use band space (ITA 2007 s13A), is the personal allowance tapered on adjusted net income including dividends (ITA 2007 s35), are the 2025/26 and 2026/27 dividend rates right, and does the additional-rate threshold sit at 125,140 GBP of taxable income

evidence.correctness: GOV.UK was not reachable from this session (www.gov.uk: proxy connect_rejected 403 on /tax-on-dividends, /income-tax-rates and /income-tax-rates/income-over-100000), so the rules are cited from my own knowledge: 2025/26 dividend rates 8.75 / 33.75 / 39.35% (ITA 2007 s8, s13), dividend allowance 500 (s13A, from 2024/25), PA 12,570 frozen, taper 1 GBP per 2 GBP of adjusted net income over 100,000 (s35), basic-rate band 37,700, additional-rate threshold 125,140 of taxable income; Autumn Budget 2025 announced the ordinary and upper dividend rates rising 2 points to 10.75 / 35.75% from 6 April 2026 with the additional rate unchanged. I wrote an independent implementation of the HMRC ordering (/tmp/claude-0/audit-ukdiv/ind.mjs: PA taper by exact half, non-savings first, PA remainder to dividends, allowance at 0% inside the bands) and compared nine cases with `node /tmp/claude-0/audit-ukdiv/ind.mjs`: dividend tax, income tax and the next-1,000 marginal cost agree to the penny on all nine, including the taper zone (100,000 + 5,000: 1,518.75 dividend tax, next 1,000 costs 537.50 = 33.75% + 20% from lost allowance), an all-dividend 150,000 straddling three bands (42,548.41), and 2026/27 across the 125,140 threshold (100,000 + 25,000: PA 70, 8,758.75, next 416.46). The only divergence is the taper uses Math.floor of the half-excess (100,000 + 1,001: PA 12,070 vs 12,069.50, income tax 27,632 vs 27,632.20), 0.20 GBP. Not a 4: rules written from memory with no fetched source and the 2026/27 rates are announced, flagged as such.
evidence.completeness: Claimed on the page and README: tax by band for 2025/26 and 2026/27 (works, split by 0/ordinary/upper/additional), dividend allowance used (works), personal allowance and taper (works, recomputed), cost of the next 1,000 (works, recomputed in and out of the taper zone), income tax on other income (works), effective rate (works), reporting checklist (present; wording issues under claims), download summary and print (wired in index.html:161-162), example and clear buttons (index.html:155-160), local opt-out usage counts with DNT/GPC (usage.mjs:34). Related-tool links all resolve to existing ventures (page.test.mjs:59). No stubs or TODOs. Served copy: `node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs uk-dividend-tax-calculator` reports no placeholder or retired origin (the github.io URL in source llms.txt is rewritten at deploy). Small product; everything it says it does, it does.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/uk-dividend-tax-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 24 tests, 24 pass, 0.12 s. Tests pin hand-derived values for the sample, PA sheltering, higher-rate salary, the taper plus additional-rate case and the 2026/27 rates. Mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: taper divisor /2 -> /4 caught; dividend allowance 500 -> 1000 caught; additional threshold 125,140 -> 150,000 caught; removing the extra income tax from lost personal allowance in the next-1,000 figure (calc.mjs:85 -> 0) SURVIVED, because both next-1,000 tests sit where the allowance is unchanged (no taper, or already zero). A fifth mutant (total <= 100000 -> <) is equivalent and not counted. Tests are the author's own expectations, but they agree with the independent implementation.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (122 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, index.html script, usage.mjs. Pure functions, a single parse that rejects missing, negative and non-numeric input with messages, no clamping, escaped HTML output, storage guarded. Defects: the marginal-cost block re-implements the whole allowance and dividend computation inline (calc.mjs:77-87, the taper formula copied from line 59) instead of calling a shared helper with dividends + 1000, and recomputes `base` (line 84) which equals chargedSlice.tax; `topRate` (line 74) is computed and returned but used nowhere; the money formatter is duplicated as gbp in index.html:126; Number() accepts ' ' (becomes 0), '1e5' and '0x10' via the API (the browser number input limits this on the page).
evidence.claims: Backed: FAQ rates and threshold (index.html:95, 97) match calc.mjs YEARS and my sources; 'allowance still uses band space' (index.html:99) matches calc.mjs:68 and is right in law; 'withdrawn 1 for every 2 over 100,000' matches line 59; 'nothing is uploaded' (page.test.mjs:16-21 bans fetch/XHR/beacon, no remote scripts); usage events named in the footer match the code (page.test.mjs:41); disclaimer and no-warranty present on index.html:109 and README; 2026/27 flagged 'announced rates' in the year picker and a finding; unmodelled items listed on page and in every result. Partly backed: the obligation 'Report on a Self Assessment return' appears whenever any dividend is charged (600 GBP of dividends over a 13,070 salary: 8.75 GBP tax, SA and payments-on-account rows both shown); GOV.UK's guidance is that dividends between 500 and 10,000 can be reported by contacting HMRC or via a tax code change and SA is required over 10,000; the row's text does mention the PAYE route, and the payments-on-account row is conditional text ('if over 1,000') shown regardless of the bill. VENTURE.yaml comment says rules written from memory and the header says 'written from HMRC's published rules without a live lookup', which is honest.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a director on a 12,570 salary deciding how much dividend to take (sample: 40,000 -> 4,031.25, next 1,000 at 337.50, so they can see where the higher-rate band starts), and a 100k-earner checking a 5,000 dividend (sees the taper warning and the 53.75% marginal cost). For the plain salary-plus-dividends case it answers the question in seconds and shows its working by band. Gaps an adviser hits in the first hour, all disclosed on the page: savings interest (which sits between non-savings and dividend income and can push dividends up a band; the personal savings allowance and starting rate are absent), relief-at-source pension contributions and Gift Aid extending the basic-rate band and reducing adjusted net income for the taper, Scottish taxpayers (non-savings income at Scottish bands; dividend bands use UK limits), and no salary-vs-dividend comparison (not claimed; listed as unbuilt in VENTURE.yaml).
evidence.domain: Compared against ITA 2007 ss.8, 13, 13A, 16 and 35 and HMRC's published worked examples as I know them (not fetched): ordering, allowance-in-band treatment, taper and band limits all follow the standard. Departures: the taper floors the half-excess (calc.mjs:59, 79), worth at most about 0.20 GBP; 'adjusted net income' is approximated by other + dividends with no deduction for gross pension contributions or Gift Aid (disclosed); the reporting checklist simplifies the 10,000 GBP SA threshold and omits the 5 October registration deadline for someone new to Self Assessment. A CTA would accept this as a correct quick estimate for the stated scope.

defects.what: No test covers the next-1,000 figure inside the personal-allowance taper zone: deleting the extra income tax from lost allowance (calc.mjs:85 -> 0) leaves all 24 tests green, so the 537.50 vs 337.50 difference a 100k earner sees is unpinned.

Reporting checklist shows 'Report on a Self Assessment return' and 'Check payments on account' for any charged dividend (8.75 GBP of tax on 600 GBP of dividends shows both); GOV.UK allows dividends of 500-10,000 to be reported by contacting HMRC or via a tax code, and payments on account only arise when the bill exceeds 1,000 and under 80% is collected at source. The text hedges, but the row titles overstate. The 5 October registration deadline for new SA filers is not mentioned.
Personal allowance taper floors the half-excess (Math.floor) where ITA 2007 s35 reduces by exactly one-half; differs by at most about 0.20 GBP of tax.

Savings interest, pension/Gift Aid band extension and adjusted-net-income deductions, and Scottish non-savings bands are not modelled; all common for the director audience. Disclosed on the page and in every result.

Marginal-cost block re-implements the allowance and dividend computation inline (taper formula copied from line 59, base recomputing chargedSlice.tax); topRate is computed but unused; the money formatter is duplicated as gbp in index.html:126.
parse() accepts a whitespace string as 0 with no error and accepts '1e5' and '0x10' via Number(); the page's number inputs limit this in the browser, but the exported compute() does not.

Rates and thresholds were written from memory with no fetched source (calc.mjs:3 says so) and the 2026/27 rates are an announcement; each result tells the user to verify, but no file records a check against the enacted text.

verdict: A small, correct tool. An independent implementation of the HMRC ordering (non-savings first, personal allowance remainder to dividends, the 500 dividend allowance at 0% inside the bands, taper over 100,000, 125,140 additional threshold) agrees with it to the penny on nine cases across both years, including the taper zone and the 2026/27 rates across the additional threshold; the only departure is a floored taper worth about 0.20. 24 tests pass and catch 3 of 4 seeded mutants; the survivor is the lost-allowance part of the next-1,000 figure, which no test pins. The page claims nothing it does not do, flags the 2026/27 rates as announced, and lists what it leaves out (savings income, band extensions, Scottish bands), which are the gaps a tax adviser would hit first. The reporting checklist overstates Self Assessment for small dividend bills. Meets the bar at 3 on every dimension; GOV.UK could not be fetched from this session, so the rule checks rest on the auditor's own knowledge.
